Echoes of Antiquity
Decoding Six Pivotal Questions of Our Past

sections.title: Page 2
sections.text:
The Past
Speaks in Clues.
History is not a collection of facts, but a
series of questions. By exploring the tools,
technologies, and ideas of ancient peoples,
we learn to decode the silent clues they
left behind. This journey examines six
pivotal inquiries that reveal humanity’s
greatest turning points—from the first
tools that shaped our world to the ideas
that connected it.

Two Paths to the Past
I. Relative Dating
Tells us if an object is older or younger than
another, without a specific calendar date.
Key Methods:
¢ Stratigraphy: The Law of Superposition.
Deeper layers are older.
© Typology: Tracking the evolution of artifact
styles (e.g., pottery, sculpture).
Seriation: Ordering artifacts based on the
changing frequency of a style.

Copper melts at ~1085°C, a
temperature achievable in early
clay furnaces. Iron melts at
~1538°C, requiring advanced
furnace technology that
developed much later.
The Chemistry
Ri
Extracting iron requires a difficult
chemical reduction process to
remove oxygen, and precise carbon
control is needed to avoid brittle
cast iron. Copper metallurgy was
far simpler.
